questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a Reorder Buffer (ROB) in modern processors?

answers.b: To enable out-of-order execution while maintaining precise interrupts

explanations.a: Cache hit rates are improved by cache design, not ROB functionality
explanations.b: Correct! ROB allows instructions to execute out-of-order while maintaining the ability to handle exceptions precisely by tracking instruction completion order
explanations.c: Branch prediction is handled by separate prediction mechanisms
explanations.d: Memory bandwidth is managed by memory controllers and cache systems

questions.question: In a processor with a Reorder Buffer, instructions are committed in which order?

explanations.a: Instructions may complete out-of-order, but commit happens in program order
explanations.b: Instructions don't have inherent priority levels in ROB
explanations.c: Correct! Even though instructions execute out-of-order, they must commit in program order to maintain precise interrupts and correct program semantics
explanations.d: Random commit order would violate program correctness

questions.question: What information is typically stored in each Reorder Buffer entry?

answers.b: Instruction type, destination register, value, and completion status
answers.c: Cache line addresses and memory mappings

explanations.a: ROB entries need much more information than just the opcode
explanations.b: Correct! ROB entries contain instruction details, destination register, computed value, and status information to track completion and enable precise commits
explanations.c: Cache and memory information is handled by separate structures
explanations.d: Branch prediction history is maintained in dedicated prediction tables

questions.question: How does the Reorder Buffer help with register renaming?

answers.b: By serving as temporary names for destination registers
answers.c: By eliminating the need for registers entirely
answers.d: By reducing the number of required registers

explanations.a: ROB entries act as temporary registers rather than providing separate physical registers
explanations.b: Correct! ROB entries serve as temporary register names, allowing multiple instructions writing to the same architectural register to coexist without conflicts
explanations.c: Registers are still essential; ROB just manages their assignment
explanations.d: ROB typically increases effective register count rather than reducing it

questions.question: What happens when an exception occurs in an instruction within the Reorder Buffer?

answers.b: All instructions are flushed from the pipeline
answers.c: The exception is noted but handled only when the instruction reaches the head of ROB

explanations.a: Immediate handling would not maintain precise interrupt semantics
explanations.b: Only younger instructions (after the exception) are flushed
explanations.c: Correct! Exceptions are recorded but only handled when the faulting instruction becomes eligible for commit, ensuring precise interrupts
explanations.d: Automatic retry is not the standard exception handling mechanism

questions.question: In the context of ROB, what does 'precise interrupt' mean?

answers.a: Interrupts occur at exact time intervals
answers.b: The processor state appears as if instructions executed in program order
answers.c: Interrupts have higher priority than regular instructions

explanations.a: Precise interrupts refer to program state, not timing precision
explanations.b: Correct! Precise interrupts ensure that when an exception occurs, the processor state reflects sequential execution up to the faulting instruction
explanations.c: This describes interrupt priority, not precision
explanations.d: Handler speed is not related to interrupt precision

questions.question: What is the main advantage of allowing out-of-order execution in processors?

answers.c: Better utilization of functional units and higher instruction throughput

explanations.a: Out-of-order execution typically increases power consumption due to complexity
explanations.b: Out-of-order execution significantly complicates processor design
explanations.c: Correct! By allowing independent instructions to execute when their operands are ready, functional units stay busy and overall throughput increases
explanations.d: Out-of-order execution requires additional hardware, increasing chip area

questions.question: Which type of dependency can be eliminated by register renaming in conjunction with ROB?

explanations.a: True data dependencies must be respected and cannot be eliminated
explanations.b: Correct! Register renaming eliminates false dependencies (WAR and WAW) by providing separate storage locations for different writes to the same architectural register
explanations.c: Control dependencies require separate mechanisms like branch prediction
explanations.d: Memory dependencies need different techniques like memory disambiguation

questions.question: What determines the maximum number of instructions that can be 'in-flight' simultaneously in a processor with ROB?

answers.c: The size of the Reorder Buffer

explanations.a: Cache size affects memory performance but not instruction capacity
explanations.b: Functional units determine execution parallelism but not total in-flight capacity
explanations.c: Correct! The ROB size directly limits how many instructions can be issued and pending completion simultaneously
explanations.d: Processor frequency affects speed but not the number of concurrent instructions
